title: Provisioning log subscription could deadlock and race channel close
root_cause: Subscriber replay was synchronously pushed into a fixed buffer and unsubscribe closed channels while Log could still send
trigger: History greater than subscriber buffer or concurrent unsubscribe/logging
consequence: Provisioning could hang or panic during ordinary progress reporting
recommendation: Collapse logging to one thread-safe history interface; remove unused subscription fanout
acceptance: No subscriber lifecycle remains; concurrent logging is race-free

title: Provisioning SSH command output was unbounded and errors could include secret-bearing command text
evidence: Static trace plus bounded-output regression harness
root_cause: Remote stdout/stderr were fully buffered and command text was embedded in errors
consequence: Memory growth and credential material could enter errors
recommendation: Bound captured output and return redacted execution errors
acceptance: At most configured output bytes retained; errors omit command and stderr

title: Runtime engine replacement could strand a healthy engine after new-start failure
evidence: State trace plus replacement/rollback regression tests
root_cause: Replacement stopped the current engine before the replacement had successfully started and had no restore transaction
trigger: Factory or Start failure after preflight
consequence: Healthy Tor/Psiphon runtime could be taken offline by a failed reconfiguration
recommendation: Keep the Start interface and hide transactional start/restore inside the module
acceptance: Failed replacement restores previous configuration; double failure reports both causes

title: Configuration manager exposed an unconditional persistence escape hatch beside CAS
evidence: Consumer search found no production Save/GetCopy callers; source interface inspection
root_cause: Safe CAS was optional because unconditional Save and duplicate GetCopy stayed exported
trigger: Any future internal caller choosing the bypass
consequence: Stale writers could overwrite authoritative settings and interface remained wider than necessary
recommendation: Make CAS persistence the only mutation interface and remove duplicate copy getter
acceptance: Production/tests use revisioned snapshot mutation; removed names have no consumers
verification: refactor audit checker; repository source/context checks

title: Dormant internal modules preserved duplicate privileged authority
locations: platform/system admin SSH and Linux tproxy; workflows/jobs generic runner; mobile lab ProtectSocket
evidence: Repository-wide consumer search plus topology ownership audit
root_cause: Unconsumed modules retained root/network/process authority after canonical owners had moved elsewhere
trigger: Future accidental registration or copy/paste reuse
consequence: Duplicate insecure authority and wider interfaces
recommendation: Retire proven-unconsumed modules under existing ADR deletion rules
acceptance: Files absent; topology records explicit retirement; canonical owners unchanged

title: Failover DNS resolver advertised 38 unused compatibility methods including no-ops/constants
evidence: Receiver-method census plus repository-wide reference search
root_cause: Historical compatibility surface remained exported inside an internal package after consumers disappeared
trigger: Maintenance or new callers infer unsupported capabilities from the interface
consequence: Weak locality and misleading test surface
recommendation: Delete only zero-consumer methods; preserve every active resolver behavior
acceptance: Removed methods have zero source/test/doc/governance consumers; active call sites unchanged

title: GSA relay source contained self-referential duplicate type aliases
evidence: Exact-source typecheck failed before change and passed after
root_cause: Stale compatibility aliases redeclared canonical wire types in the same package
recommendation: Remove invalid aliases and use canonical relay wire types directly

title: NAT package protocol constants collided with exported TCP/UDP listener types
evidence: Exact-source typecheck failed before change and passed after
root_cause: Protocol constants reused type identifiers in the same package namespace
recommendation: Rename protocol constants while preserving listener type interface
acceptance: All active platform selections have zero duplicate declarations; NAT tests pass

title: Authenticated serverless relay disabled TLS certificate verification
evidence: Live call trace plus self-signed-certificate rejection regression
root_cause: Diagnostic-style trust bypass leaked into an authenticated relay transport
trigger: MITM with attacker-controlled certificate on relay path
recommendation: Restore normal PKI verification on live relay traffic

title: HTTP/GSA relay close state raced concurrent I/O
locations: integrations/relayclient HTTP and GSA net.Conn adapters
evidence: Static race trace plus race harness
root_cause: Plain bool lifecycle state was accessed by concurrent methods
consequence: Data race and undefined lifecycle behavior

title: Relay failed-write rollback aliased the buffer it was rewriting
evidence: Buffer alias trace plus deterministic regression
root_cause: Bytes() slice referenced the same backing array reset and overwritten during prepend
trigger: Failed transmit with pending queued bytes
consequence: Retry could silently corrupt queued tunnel payload ordering/content
recommendation: Centralize prepend rollback and copy pending bytes before reset
acceptance: Failed payload is prepended without aliasing or corruption

title: WebTunnel used an undefined stale adapter identifier and trusted any TLS certificate by default
evidence: Exact-source compile trace plus self-signed/pin TLS harness
root_cause: Stale relay type name survived owner convergence; TLS pin logic was implemented as trust-all unless pinned
trigger: Build or live unpinned WebTunnel use
recommendation: Use canonical relay WebSocketConn; default to PKI verification; allow explicit SHA-256 pin as alternate trust mode
acceptance: Unpinned self-signed cert rejected; exact pin accepted

title: Android lab retained a duplicate obsolete ProtectSocket adapter
evidence: Cross-platform declaration checker plus zero-consumer search
root_cause: Stale lab JNI seam remained after Android/Kotlin ownership moved
consequence: Duplicate declaration and misleading alternate owner
acceptance: Android declaration selection has no duplicate top-level names

title: Repository lacked a dependency-free guard for active Go declaration integrity
evidence: Audit found multiple deterministic compile blockers while full Go 1.26 build was environment-blocked
root_cause: Canonical verification depended on unavailable full module/toolchain builds to catch basic source collisions
trigger: Offline/local verification or partially provisioned CI
consequence: Compile blockers could survive source-only verification
recommendation: Add stdlib-only syntax and cross-platform top-level declaration checker
acceptance: Linux/Windows/macOS/Android selections parse with zero duplicates

title: Both live SSH client paths disable server host-key verification
locations: provisioning SSH runner; runtime SSH tunnel
evidence: Two direct InsecureIgnoreHostKey occurrences plus request/config trace showing no trust material
root_cause: SSH trust identity is absent from the domain model, so callers cannot supply or persist expected keys
trigger: Any provisioning or SSH tunnel connection over hostile/redirected network
recommendation: Introduce one SSH host-identity seam used by both real adapters; require explicit fingerprint/known-host policy and migration semantics
acceptance: No live InsecureIgnoreHostKey; negative/rotation/mismatch tests; operator-visible trust state

title: Provisioning executes an unpinned privileged Docker bootstrap script
evidence: Direct live execution trace of curl get.docker.com piped to sh
root_cause: Bootstrap source/version/integrity are not part of the provisioning contract
trigger: Docker absent on a new host
consequence: Upstream compromise or drift executes unreviewed root code
recommendation: Choose a pinned package/repository or digest-verified installer strategy with explicit supported-host policy
acceptance: No unpinned remote script-to-shell; version/integrity evidence and rollback documented

title: Rust FFI input helper fabricates arbitrary lifetime and collapses null/invalid UTF-8 to empty input
evidence: Unsafe helper inspection; 23 helper uses; 38 unsafe extern functions; safety-doc suppression
root_cause: FFI input parsing and panic/JSON/string envelopes are repeated and the raw-string helper returns a caller-chosen lifetime
trigger: Malformed/null/invalid input or future refactor retaining returned reference
consequence: Ambiguous input errors and unnecessary unsafe lifetime surface
recommendation: Deepen behind unchanged C ABI: copy raw C input immediately into owned validated data and centralize panic/JSON/output envelope
acceptance: C ABI unchanged; null/UTF-8 errors explicit; no arbitrary-lifetime helper; safety docs and Cargo/Miri/ABI tests pass
verification: Blocked: Cargo/rustc unavailable in this environment

title: HTTP/GSA relay adapters implement net.Conn deadlines as no-ops and permit unbounded queued transmit data
root_cause: Polling relay protocol is presented as net.Conn without implementing its timeout/backpressure semantics
trigger: Slow/failed relay with sustained producer writes
consequence: Callers may wait indefinitely or accumulate memory
recommendation: Design deadline/backpressure semantics together behind the relay seam instead of patching individual methods
acceptance: Deadline tests, bounded queue behavior, cancellation and recovery tests
verification: Requires protocol behavior decision; not changed in this pass
